newsitem.title: USA: Texas power prices ease slightly despite natgas - Nov 19.
newsitem.headline: Texas power prices ease slightly despite natgas - Nov 19.

text.p: Wholesale power prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) eased slightly Tuesday despite rising natural gas prices, power brokers and marketers said.
Although short-term physical Texas gas prices surged Tuesday, the sources said mild weather in Texas held power prices steady.
Temperatures through much of Texas were forecast to reach highs in the 70-80 degrees Fahrenheit level Wednesday and Thursday, limiting electricity demand.
Texas Utilities' 1,150 megawatt Comanche Peak 1 continued to operate at limited levels as of Tuesday during restart testing from a scheduled outage.
Prices for peak, firm power for Wednesday delivery were quoted in the $24.00-26.00 range from $25.25-26.25 per megawatt hour (MWh) on Monday, the brokers and marketers said.
Off-peak non-firm ERCOT power transactions were again said to be very thin with notional quotes in the $10.00-12.00 per MWh range.
December peak power was discussed steady at $25.25-25.75, while January/February ERCOT power prices were pegged unchanged at $25.30-25.85, the sources said.
